{{Navbar-Global Gas Infrastructure Tracker}}
The '''Northern Natural Gas Pipeline''' is an operating natural gas pipeline in the United States.<ref name=source1>[http://bit.ly/2lhUaxa Northern Natural Gas Pipeline,] Wikipedia, accessed Aug. 21, 2021.</ref>

==Location==
The pipeline runs from the Permian Basin, Texas, to near Chicago, Illinois, and to Wisconsin, Minnesota, and Michigan.

==Background==

=== Main System ===
Northern Natural Gas (NNG) is a natural gas pipeline that brings gas from the Permian Basin in Texas to the Chicago area, Wisconsin, Minnesota and the Upper Peninsula of Michigan.<ref name=source1/> It is owned by Berkshire Hathaway Energy.<ref>[http://www.northernnaturalgas.com/aboutus/Pages/Overview.aspx Northern Natural Gas - About Us], Northern Natural Gas, accessed Aug. 21, 2021.</ref> Its FERC code is 59.<ref name=source1/>

=== Northern Lights 2017 Expansion ===
In January 2017, Northern Natural Gas received approval from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) to build a 2.0 mile extension in Sherburne County, Minnesota, and a 2.8 mile extension of the pipeline in Isanti County, Minnesota.<ref name="FERC">[https://web.archive.org/web/20180630075855/https://www.ferc.gov/CalendarFiles/20170130140145-CP16-472-000.pdf 158 FERC ¶ 61,079], FERC, Jan. 30, 2017, archived from [https://www.ferc.gov/CalendarFiles/20170130140145-CP16-472-000.pdf the original], archived accessed Aug. 21, 2021.</ref> The 2.0 mile extension was completed and placed in service in July 2017 and the 2.8 mile extension was completed and placed in service in October 2017.<ref name="sherop">[http://www.northernnaturalgas.com/Document%20Postings/2017_11_10_NL2017_bwkly_rpt18.pdf Northern's Biweekly Report #18], Northern Natural Gas, Nov. 17, 2017, accessed Aug. 21, 2021.</ref> The two extensions increased the pipeline's capacity by 76 mcfd.<ref name="FERC" />

=== Rochester Expansion Project ===
The Rochester Expansion Project will add capacity to the Northern Natural Gas Pipeline in Minnesota, USA. According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA), the project entered service in December of 2019.<ref name="eianov" /><ref name="ftmap" />

=== Northern Lights 2019 Expansion ===
The "Northern Lights 2019" expansion will consist of: (1) 9.9 miles of 24-inch-diameter greenfield pipeline, (2) 13.5 miles of branch line and mainline loops/extensions ranging in size from 6-inch- to 36-inch-diameter pipeline; (3) additional compression at Northern’s existing Faribault and Owatonna compressor stations; and (4) a new compressor station located near Carver, Minnesota.<ref>[http://www.northernnaturalgas.com/expansionprojects/Pages/NorthernLights2019-Rochester.aspx Northern Lights 2019 - Rochester Expansion], Northern Natural Gas, accessed January 2018</ref>

According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA), as of January 2020, the project was partially complete and is expected to go into service in 2020.<ref name="eianov" /><ref name="ftmap" />

=== Northern Lights 2021 Expansion ===
The Northern Lights 2021 expansion project will include new looping, extension of existing lines, a new compressor station, and modifications to an existing compressor. Developers applied for approval with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) in July, 2020.<ref name="eia1021" /> In May 2021, FERC issued a certificate for the pipeline's construction.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ferc.gov/media/c-2-cp20-503-000-052021|title=C-2-CP20-503-000-052021 {{!}} Federal Energy Regulatory Commission|website=www.ferc.gov|language=en|access-date=2021-12-05}}</ref>

The project was completed in December 2022.<ref name="eia1021" />

=== Northern Lights 2023 Expansion ===
The 2023 expansion involves additional pipeline and facilities installed in various Minnesota and Wisconsin counties to expand capacity to the Northern Market Area, United States.<ref name="eia1021" />

The project was completed in October 2024.<ref name="eia1021" />

=== A-Line Replacement Project ===
Abandon 87 miles of A-line and replace its capacity with six mile extension to its existing D-Line in Wright County, Iowa. This was later reduced to 1.51 miles. The project was complete October 2023.<ref name="eia1021" />

=== Lake City 1st Branch Line Abandonment and Capacity Replacement Project ===
Abandon aging existing line and and replace lost capacity by uprating existing lines, and building a new pipeline segment. Once the Lake City 2nd branch line is in-service, the Lake City 1st line branch will be abandoned in Q2 2023.<ref name="eia1021" /> 

The project was completed in 2022.<ref name="eia1021" />

=== C-Line Replacement Project ===
Abandon in place part of Northern Natural A-Line (approx 29.63 miles of 16-inch diameter line) and construct and operate approx 9.07-mile extension of 20-inch diameter C-Line.<ref name="eia1021" />

The project was completed in 2023.<ref name="eia1021" />

=== South Sioux City to Sioux Falls A-line Replacement Project ===
Replacement of lines that runs between South Dakota and Nebraska.<ref name="eia1021" />

The project was completed in 2024.<ref name="eia1021" />

=== Tarzan Compressor Station Project ===
Project is to install and operate a new 11,152-HP compressor station in Andrews County, TX. Project will provide 87,000 Dth/day of new transportation capacity in growing Permian Basin. If approved, the project expects to complete in 2026.<ref name="eia1021" /> 

=== Northern Lights 2025 Expansion ===
Project is 4 extensions of branch lines of varying lengths and diameter pipe; minor modifications to the existing La Crescent CS, and above ground facilities. Project also includes removing approx 275 feet of an existing branch line. Project is to serve residential, commercial and industrial market growth in Northern's market area.<ref name="eia1021" />
